newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - October 8.

text.p: Following are the highlights of stories reported in the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Only the IRA has the type of explosives and the ability to carry out the attack which rocked the British army headquarters in Northern Ireland on Monday, senior security sources believe.
- The ceasefire by pro-British Loyalist guerrillas was balanced on a knife-edge after the Lisburn bomb, for which there was no warning or admission of responsibility.

- Irish Minister for Foreign Affairs Dick Spring, who is on a whistle-stop peace tour of the Middle East, called on Monday for "concrete steps" to show that the Middle East peace process was still on track.

- The National Economic and Social Council (NESC) is to call for a strategy of wage moderation in return for tax concessions in the conclusions of a major report on the Irish economy to be published on Monday.
- The Wellworth supermarket chain, a unit of Irish investment firm Fitzwilton, is to open three new stores in Northern Ireland worth 30 million Irish pounds.
- Irish media group Independent Newspapers was forced on Monday to increase its bid for New Zealand publishing firm Wilson & Horton to NZ$11, to ensure the support of W&H's board.
- Peace hopes were virtually demolished on Monday night after two car bombs exploded inside the high-security British army base at Lisburn, County Armagh, injuring 31 soldiers and civilians.
- A four-year-old Irish girl who was believed to have been kidnapped from a Florida hotel, was found safe and well on Monday after a massive police search.
- Dublin man, John Gilligan who is a self-confessed suspect in the murder of Irish journalist Veronica Guerin, appears in court in Britain today to face drug trafficking charges.
- Sterling's recent rally could take it above 2.6 marks and cause serious problems for Ireland's anti-inflationary policy, British economist Roger Bootle said.
- Irish pension funds performed strongly on the back of buoyant bond and equity markets in the third quarter of 1996, a survey said on Monday.
